model_expansion.en: A specified Fermat model M of exponent N consists of an intermediate field K between ℚ and an algebraic closure of ℚ(X), elements u,v∈K with u transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, K finite-dimensional over ℚ(u), and [K:ℚ(u)]=N. The readbacks quantify over supplied models and do not assert that a model exists.
model_expansion.zh_Hans: 指数为 N 的给定 Fermat 模型 M 包含有理数域与 ℚ(X) 的代数闭包之间的中间域 K，以及元素 u,v∈K，满足 u 关于有理数域超越、u^N+v^N=1、ℚ(u,v)=K、K 在 ℚ(u) 上有限维且 [K:ℚ(u)]=N。读回量化的是已给定模型，不断言模型存在。
model_expansion.ja: 指数 N の指定された Fermat 模型 M は、有理数体と ℚ(X) の代数閉包との間の中間体 K、および元 u,v∈K からなり、u は有理数体上超越的であり、u^N+v^N=1、ℚ(u,v)=K、K は ℚ(u) 上有限次元かつ [K:ℚ(u)]=N を満たす。読戻しは与えられた模型について量化し、模型の存在は主張しない。

notation.en: κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P; deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P); a divisor is a finite-support function P↦A(P)∈ℤ; its degree is Σ_P A(P)deg(P); effectiveness means A(P)≥0 for every P; pole multiplicity is max(0,−ord_P(f)), including f=0.
notation.zh_Hans: κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P；deg(P) 是剩余域在有理数域上的自然数值有限秩；除子是有限支撑整数值函数 P↦A(P)，其次数为 Σ_P A(P)deg(P)；有效指每处的系数非负；极点重数为 max(0,−ord_P(f))，也包括零函数。
notation.ja: κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P、deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P) とする。因子は有限台の整数値関数 P↦A(P) であり、その次数は Σ_P A(P)deg(P) である。有効とは全ての係数が非負であることをいう。極の重複度は零関数も含め max(0,−ord_P(f)) である。

M.en: For every N∈ℕ and every specified Fermat model M of exponent N,
M.zh: 对任意自然数 N 及任意给定的指数为 N 的 Fermat 模型 M，
M.ja: 任意の自然数 N と指数 N の指定された任意の Fermat 模型 M に対して、

MD.en: For every N∈ℕ, every specified Fermat model M, and every proof hDVR that all places of M.K have discrete valuation rings, write L(A) for {f∈M.K | f=0 or ord_P(f)≥−A(P) at every place P}, and ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A). Write (f), (f)₀ and (f)∞ for the finite-support divisors with coefficients ord_P(f), max(0,ord_P(f)) and max(0,−ord_P(f)), respectively; deg denotes the residue-degree-weighted divisor degree.
MD.zh: 对任意自然数 N、任意给定 Fermat 模型 M 以及其每个处的赋值环均为离散赋值环的证明 hDVR，记 L(A)={f∈M.K | f=0 或对每个处 P 都有 ord_P(f)≥−A(P)}，ℓ(A) 为 L(A) 在有理数域上的自然数值有限秩。记 (f)、(f)₀、(f)∞ 分别为逐处系数为 ord_P(f)、max(0,ord_P(f))、max(0,−ord_P(f)) 的有限支撑除子，deg 为按剩余域次数加权的除子次数。
MD.ja: 任意の自然数 N、指定された任意の Fermat 模型 M、および全ての素点の付値環が離散付値環であることの任意の証明 hDVR を取る。L(A)={f∈M.K | f=0 または全ての素点 P で ord_P(f)≥−A(P)}、ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A) と書く。(f)、(f)₀、(f)∞ を、それぞれ各素点での係数が ord_P(f)、max(0,ord_P(f))、max(0,−ord_P(f)) となる有限台の因子とし、deg を剰余体の次数で重みを付けた因子の次数とする。

P.en: Let K be any field of characteristic zero and P any place, represented by its proper valuation subring O_P containing ℚ.
P.zh: 设 K 为任意特征零域，P 为任意处，其赋值环 O_P 是包含有理数域的真赋值子环。
P.ja: K を任意の標数零の体とし、P を有理数体を含む真の付値部分環 O_P で表される任意の素点とする。

readbacks.en: For every natural number N and every given model M, let K=M.K be an intermediate field between ℚ and a fixed algebraic closure of the rational function field ℚ(X). The model supplies u,v∈K such that u is transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, K is finite-dimensional over ℚ(u), and [K:ℚ(u)]=N. A place P of K is a valuation subring O_P properly contained in K and containing the image of every rational number. Write 𝔪_P for its maximal ideal, κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P for its residue field, and the residue map for the quotient homomorphism O_P→κ(P). A divisor A is a function from all places of K to ℤ with finite support; inequalities between divisors mean inequalities of every coefficient, and A is effective if A(P)≥0 for every place P. Write deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P) and deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P), with the residue degrees cast to integers. Here Module.finrank is the natural-number-valued finite rank, which is the usual vector-space dimension when finite-dimensionality holds. For a place with discrete valuation ring O_P, ord_P(f) denotes the normalized integer order of f, positive on nonzero elements of 𝔪_P and negative on poles; its value at zero is defined to be ord_P(0)=0. Equivalently ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)), where v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ is the normalized multiplicative valuation, ℤᵐ⁰ is the multiplicative copy of ℤ with an added zero, and log and exp are the formal maps for this notation, not real analytic functions. Supply any proof hDVR that O_P is a discrete valuation ring for every place P of K. For each divisor A define the ℚ-subspace L(A)={f∈K | f=0 or ord_P(f)≥−A(P) for every place P} and ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A). Write (f), (f)₀ and (f)∞ for the finite-support divisors of coefficients ord_P(f), max(0,ord_P(f)) and max(0,−ord_P(f)), respectively; these are the principal divisor, zero divisor and pole divisor of f. By the order convention all three divisors of the zero function are the zero divisor whose coefficients are all zero. Write [P] for the divisor of coefficient one at P and zero elsewhere. For every f∈M.K, define its finite-support principal divisor (f) to have coefficient ord_P(f) at every place P.
readbacks.zh_Hans: 对任意自然数 N 和任意给定模型 M，令 K=M.K 为有理数域与有理函数域 ℚ(X) 的一个固定代数闭包之间的中间域。模型给定 u,v∈K，满足 u 关于有理数域超越、u^N+v^N=1、ℚ(u,v)=K、K 在 ℚ(u) 上有限维且 [K:ℚ(u)]=N。K 的一个处 P 指包含所有有理数的像且真包含于 K 的赋值子环 O_P。记 𝔪_P 为其极大理想，κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P 为其剩余域，剩余映射指商同态 O_P→κ(P)。除子 A 指 K 的全部处上的有限支撑整数值函数；除子不等式指每个处的系数不等式，若每个处 P 都满足 A(P)≥0，则称 A 有效。记 deg(P) 为剩余域 κ(P) 在有理数域上的自然数值有限秩，deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P)，其中剩余域次数先转为整数。自然数值有限秩在空间有限维时等于通常的向量空间维数。当处 P 的赋值环 O_P 为离散赋值环时，ord_P(f) 表示函数 f 的正规化整数阶，在极大理想的非零元素上为正、在极点处为负，并约定 ord_P(0)=0。等价地 ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f))，其中 v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ 为正规化乘法赋值，ℤᵐ⁰ 是整数加法群改写为乘法记法后再添零元的构造，log 与 exp 是该记法的形式映射，并非实数解析函数。另给定证明 hDVR，断言每个处 P 的赋值环 O_P 都是离散赋值环。对每个除子 A，定义有理数线性子空间 L(A)={f∈K | f=0 或每个处 P 都满足 ord_P(f)≥−A(P)}，并记 ℓ(A) 为 L(A) 在有理数域上的自然数值有限秩。记 (f)、(f)₀、(f)∞ 分别为逐处系数为 ord_P(f)、max(0,ord_P(f))、max(0,−ord_P(f)) 的有限支撑除子，分别称主除子、零点除子、极点除子。按阶的约定，零函数的这三个除子都等于所有系数均为零的零除子。记 [P] 为在 P 处系数为一且其余系数为零的除子。对每个 f∈M.K，将其主除子 (f) 定义为在每个处 P 的系数为 ord_P(f) 的有限支撑除子。
readbacks.ja: 任意の自然数 N と与えられた任意の模型 M に対し、K=M.K を有理数体と有理関数体 ℚ(X) の固定された代数閉包との間の中間体とする。模型は u,v∈K を与え、u は有理数体上超越的であり、u^N+v^N=1、ℚ(u,v)=K、K は ℚ(u) 上有限次元かつ [K:ℚ(u)]=N を満たす。K の素点 P とは、全ての有理数の像を含み K に真に含まれる付値部分環 O_P をいう。𝔪_P をその極大イデアル、κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P を剰余体とし、剰余写像は商準同型 O_P→κ(P) を表す。因子 A とは K の全ての素点上の有限台を持つ整数値関数である。因子の不等式は各係数の不等式を表し、全ての素点 P で A(P)≥0 なら A を有効という。deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P)、deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P) と書き、剰余体の次数は整数に型変換する。Module.finrank は自然数値の有限階数であり、空間が有限次元なら通常のベクトル空間の次元と一致する。O_P が離散付値環である素点では、ord_P(f) は f の正規化された整数値の位数を表し、極大イデアルの非零元では正、極では負となり、ord_P(0)=0 と定める。同値な表示は ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)) である。v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ は正規化された乗法的付値、ℤᵐ⁰ は整数の加法群を乗法的に書き零元を加えたものであり、log と exp はこの記法の形式的な写像であって実解析の関数ではない。全ての素点 P で O_P が離散付値環であることの任意の証明 hDVR を指定する。各因子 A に対し、有理数線形部分空間 L(A)={f∈K | f=0 または全ての素点 P で ord_P(f)≥−A(P)} を定め、ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A) と書く。(f)、(f)₀、(f)∞ をそれぞれ各素点での係数が ord_P(f)、max(0,ord_P(f))、max(0,−ord_P(f)) となる有限台の因子とし、主因子、零点の因子、極の因子と呼ぶ。位数の規約により、零関数のこれら三つの因子は全ての係数が零である零因子となる。[P] は P での係数が一で他では零である因子を表す。任意の f∈M.K に対し、その主因子 (f) を各素点 P での係数が ord_P(f) となる有限台の因子と定める。

The model supplies u,v∈K such that u is transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, K is finite-dimensional over ℚ(u), and [K:ℚ(u)]=N. A place P of K is a valuation subring O_P properly contained in K and containing the image of every rational number. Write 𝔪_P for its maximal ideal, κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P for its residue field, and the residue map for the quotient homomorphism O_P→κ(P). A divisor A is a function from all places of K to ℤ with finite support; inequalities between divisors mean inequalities of every coefficient, and A is effective if A(P)≥0 for every place P. Write deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P) and deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P), with the residue degrees cast to integers. Here Module.finrank is the natural-number-valued finite rank, which is the usual vector-space dimension when finite-dimensionality holds. For a place with discrete valuation ring O_P, ord_P(f) denotes the normalized integer order of f, positive on nonzero elements of 𝔪_P and negative on poles; its value at zero is defined to be ord_P(0)=0. Equivalently ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)), where v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ is the normalized multiplicative valuation, ℤᵐ⁰ is the multiplicative copy of ℤ with an added zero, and log and exp are the formal maps for this notation, not real analytic functions. Supply any proof hDVR that O_P is a discrete valuation ring for every place P of K. For each divisor A define the ℚ-subspace L(A)={f∈K | f=0 or ord_P(f)≥−A(P) for every place P} and ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A). Write (f), (f)₀ and (f)∞ for the finite-support divisors of coefficients ord_P(f), max(0,ord_P(f)) and max(0,−ord_P(f)), respectively; these are the principal divisor, zero divisor and pole divisor of f. By the order convention all three divisors of the zero function are the zero divisor whose coefficients are all zero. Write [P] for the divisor of coefficient one at P and zero elsewhere. For every f∈M.K and place P, (f)₀(P)=max(0,ord_P(f)).
readbacks.zh_Hans: 对任意自然数 N 和任意给定模型 M，令 K=M.K 为有理数域与有理函数域 ℚ(X) 的一个固定代数闭包之间的中间域。模型给定 u,v∈K，满足 u 关于有理数域超越、u^N+v^N=1、ℚ(u,v)=K、K 在 ℚ(u) 上有限维且 [K:ℚ(u)]=N。K 的一个处 P 指包含所有有理数的像且真包含于 K 的赋值子环 O_P。记 𝔪_P 为其极大理想，κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P 为其剩余域，剩余映射指商同态 O_P→κ(P)。除子 A 指 K 的全部处上的有限支撑整数值函数；除子不等式指每个处的系数不等式，若每个处 P 都满足 A(P)≥0，则称 A 有效。记 deg(P) 为剩余域 κ(P) 在有理数域上的自然数值有限秩，deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P)，其中剩余域次数先转为整数。自然数值有限秩在空间有限维时等于通常的向量空间维数。当处 P 的赋值环 O_P 为离散赋值环时，ord_P(f) 表示函数 f 的正规化整数阶，在极大理想的非零元素上为正、在极点处为负，并约定 ord_P(0)=0。等价地 ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f))，其中 v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ 为正规化乘法赋值，ℤᵐ⁰ 是整数加法群改写为乘法记法后再添零元的构造，log 与 exp 是该记法的形式映射，并非实数解析函数。另给定证明 hDVR，断言每个处 P 的赋值环 O_P 都是离散赋值环。对每个除子 A，定义有理数线性子空间 L(A)={f∈K | f=0 或每个处 P 都满足 ord_P(f)≥−A(P)}，并记 ℓ(A) 为 L(A) 在有理数域上的自然数值有限秩。记 (f)、(f)₀、(f)∞ 分别为逐处系数为 ord_P(f)、max(0,ord_P(f))、max(0,−ord_P(f)) 的有限支撑除子，分别称主除子、零点除子、极点除子。按阶的约定，零函数的这三个除子都等于所有系数均为零的零除子。记 [P] 为在 P 处系数为一且其余系数为零的除子。对每个 f∈M.K 及处 P，有 (f)₀(P)=max(0,ord_P(f))。
readbacks.ja: 任意の自然数 N と与えられた任意の模型 M に対し、K=M.K を有理数体と有理関数体 ℚ(X) の固定された代数閉包との間の中間体とする。模型は u,v∈K を与え、u は有理数体上超越的であり、u^N+v^N=1、ℚ(u,v)=K、K は ℚ(u) 上有限次元かつ [K:ℚ(u)]=N を満たす。K の素点 P とは、全ての有理数の像を含み K に真に含まれる付値部分環 O_P をいう。𝔪_P をその極大イデアル、κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P を剰余体とし、剰余写像は商準同型 O_P→κ(P) を表す。因子 A とは K の全ての素点上の有限台を持つ整数値関数である。因子の不等式は各係数の不等式を表し、全ての素点 P で A(P)≥0 なら A を有効という。deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P)、deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P) と書き、剰余体の次数は整数に型変換する。Module.finrank は自然数値の有限階数であり、空間が有限次元なら通常のベクトル空間の次元と一致する。O_P が離散付値環である素点では、ord_P(f) は f の正規化された整数値の位数を表し、極大イデアルの非零元では正、極では負となり、ord_P(0)=0 と定める。同値な表示は ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)) である。v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ は正規化された乗法的付値、ℤᵐ⁰ は整数の加法群を乗法的に書き零元を加えたものであり、log と exp はこの記法の形式的な写像であって実解析の関数ではない。全ての素点 P で O_P が離散付値環であることの任意の証明 hDVR を指定する。各因子 A に対し、有理数線形部分空間 L(A)={f∈K | f=0 または全ての素点 P で ord_P(f)≥−A(P)} を定め、ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A) と書く。(f)、(f)₀、(f)∞ をそれぞれ各素点での係数が ord_P(f)、max(0,ord_P(f))、max(0,−ord_P(f)) となる有限台の因子とし、主因子、零点の因子、極の因子と呼ぶ。位数の規約により、零関数のこれら三つの因子は全ての係数が零である零因子となる。[P] は P での係数が一で他では零である因子を表す。任意の f∈M.K と素点 P に対し、(f)₀(P)=max(0,ord_P(f)) である。

theorem functionPoleDivisor_apply (M : Model N) (hDVR : PlacesDiscrete M)
    (f : M.K) (P : Place M.K) : functionPoleDivisor M hDVR f P = max 0 (-ord M hDVR P f)

    (f : M.K) (P : Place M.K) : functionPoleDivisor M hDVR f P = max 0 (-ord M hDVR P f)

readbacks.en: For every natural number N and every given model M, let K=M.K be an intermediate field between ℚ and a fixed algebraic closure of the rational function field ℚ(X). The model supplies u,v∈K such that u is transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, K is finite-dimensional over ℚ(u), and [K:ℚ(u)]=N. A place P of K is a valuation subring O_P properly contained in K and containing the image of every rational number. Write 𝔪_P for its maximal ideal, κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P for its residue field, and the residue map for the quotient homomorphism O_P→κ(P). A divisor A is a function from all places of K to ℤ with finite support; inequalities between divisors mean inequalities of every coefficient, and A is effective if A(P)≥0 for every place P. Write deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P) and deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P), with the residue degrees cast to integers. Here Module.finrank is the natural-number-valued finite rank, which is the usual vector-space dimension when finite-dimensionality holds. For a place with discrete valuation ring O_P, ord_P(f) denotes the normalized integer order of f, positive on nonzero elements of 𝔪_P and negative on poles; its value at zero is defined to be ord_P(0)=0. Equivalently ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)), where v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ is the normalized multiplicative valuation, ℤᵐ⁰ is the multiplicative copy of ℤ with an added zero, and log and exp are the formal maps for this notation, not real analytic functions. Supply any proof hDVR that O_P is a discrete valuation ring for every place P of K. For each divisor A define the ℚ-subspace L(A)={f∈K | f=0 or ord_P(f)≥−A(P) for every place P} and ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A). Write (f), (f)₀ and (f)∞ for the finite-support divisors of coefficients ord_P(f), max(0,ord_P(f)) and max(0,−ord_P(f)), respectively; these are the principal divisor, zero divisor and pole divisor of f. By the order convention all three divisors of the zero function are the zero divisor whose coefficients are all zero. Write [P] for the divisor of coefficient one at P and zero elsewhere. For every f∈M.K, (f)=(f)₀−(f)∞.

readbacks.en: For every natural number N and every given model M, let K=M.K be an intermediate field between ℚ and a fixed algebraic closure of the rational function field ℚ(X). The model supplies u,v∈K such that u is transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, K is finite-dimensional over ℚ(u), and [K:ℚ(u)]=N. A place P of K is a valuation subring O_P properly contained in K and containing the image of every rational number. Write 𝔪_P for its maximal ideal, κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P for its residue field, and the residue map for the quotient homomorphism O_P→κ(P). A divisor A is a function from all places of K to ℤ with finite support; inequalities between divisors mean inequalities of every coefficient, and A is effective if A(P)≥0 for every place P. Write deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P) and deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P), with the residue degrees cast to integers. Here Module.finrank is the natural-number-valued finite rank, which is the usual vector-space dimension when finite-dimensionality holds. For a place with discrete valuation ring O_P, ord_P(f) denotes the normalized integer order of f, positive on nonzero elements of 𝔪_P and negative on poles; its value at zero is defined to be ord_P(0)=0. Equivalently ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)), where v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ is the normalized multiplicative valuation, ℤᵐ⁰ is the multiplicative copy of ℤ with an added zero, and log and exp are the formal maps for this notation, not real analytic functions. Supply any proof hDVR that O_P is a discrete valuation ring for every place P of K. For each divisor A define the ℚ-subspace L(A)={f∈K | f=0 or ord_P(f)≥−A(P) for every place P} and ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A). The basis pole correction C is effective.

readbacks.en: For every natural number N and every given model M, let K=M.K be an intermediate field between ℚ and a fixed algebraic closure of the rational function field ℚ(X). The model supplies u,v∈K such that u is transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, K is finite-dimensional over ℚ(u), and [K:ℚ(u)]=N. A place P of K is a valuation subring O_P properly contained in K and containing the image of every rational number. Write 𝔪_P for its maximal ideal, κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P for its residue field, and the residue map for the quotient homomorphism O_P→κ(P). A divisor A is a function from all places of K to ℤ with finite support; inequalities between divisors mean inequalities of every coefficient, and A is effective if A(P)≥0 for every place P. Write deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P) and deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P), with the residue degrees cast to integers. Here Module.finrank is the natural-number-valued finite rank, which is the usual vector-space dimension when finite-dimensionality holds. For a place with discrete valuation ring O_P, ord_P(f) denotes the normalized integer order of f, positive on nonzero elements of 𝔪_P and negative on poles; its value at zero is defined to be ord_P(0)=0. Equivalently ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)), where v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ is the normalized multiplicative valuation, ℤᵐ⁰ is the multiplicative copy of ℤ with an added zero, and log and exp are the formal maps for this notation, not real analytic functions. Supply any proof hDVR that O_P is a discrete valuation ring for every place P of K. For each divisor A define the ℚ-subspace L(A)={f∈K | f=0 or ord_P(f)≥−A(P) for every place P} and ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A). Also supply a curve-field instance, meaning that there exists s∈K transcendental over ℚ with K finite-dimensional over ℚ(s). Write (f), (f)₀ and (f)∞ for the finite-support divisors of coefficients ord_P(f), max(0,ord_P(f)) and max(0,−ord_P(f)), respectively; these are the principal divisor, zero divisor and pole divisor of f. By the order convention all three divisors of the zero function are the zero divisor whose coefficients are all zero. Write [P] for the divisor of coefficient one at P and zero elsewhere. For every divisor A and f∈M.K, f∈L(A) if and only if f=0 or −A(P)≤P.ord(f) at every place P.

readbacks.en: For every natural number N and every given model M, let K=M.K be an intermediate field between ℚ and a fixed algebraic closure of the rational function field ℚ(X). The model supplies u,v∈K such that u is transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, K is finite-dimensional over ℚ(u), and [K:ℚ(u)]=N. A place P of K is a valuation subring O_P properly contained in K and containing the image of every rational number. Write 𝔪_P for its maximal ideal, κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P for its residue field, and the residue map for the quotient homomorphism O_P→κ(P). A divisor A is a function from all places of K to ℤ with finite support; inequalities between divisors mean inequalities of every coefficient, and A is effective if A(P)≥0 for every place P. Write deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P) and deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P), with the residue degrees cast to integers. Here Module.finrank is the natural-number-valued finite rank, which is the usual vector-space dimension when finite-dimensionality holds. For a place with discrete valuation ring O_P, ord_P(f) denotes the normalized integer order of f, positive on nonzero elements of 𝔪_P and negative on poles; its value at zero is defined to be ord_P(0)=0. Equivalently ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)), where v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ is the normalized multiplicative valuation, ℤᵐ⁰ is the multiplicative copy of ℤ with an added zero, and log and exp are the formal maps for this notation, not real analytic functions. Supply any proof hDVR that O_P is a discrete valuation ring for every place P of K. For each divisor A define the ℚ-subspace L(A)={f∈K | f=0 or ord_P(f)≥−A(P) for every place P} and ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A). Also supply a curve-field instance, meaning that there exists s∈K transcendental over ℚ with K finite-dimensional over ℚ(s). Write (f), (f)₀ and (f)∞ for the finite-support divisors of coefficients ord_P(f), max(0,ord_P(f)) and max(0,−ord_P(f)), respectively; these are the principal divisor, zero divisor and pole divisor of f. By the order convention all three divisors of the zero function are the zero divisor whose coefficients are all zero. Write [P] for the divisor of coefficient one at P and zero elsewhere. For every divisor A and nonzero z∈M.K, multiplication by z defines a ℚ-linear equivalence L(A+(z))≃L(A), with inverse multiplication by z⁻¹.

readbacks.en: For every natural number N and every given model M, let K=M.K be an intermediate field between ℚ and a fixed algebraic closure of the rational function field ℚ(X). The model supplies u,v∈K such that u is transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, K is finite-dimensional over ℚ(u), and [K:ℚ(u)]=N. A place P of K is a valuation subring O_P properly contained in K and containing the image of every rational number. Write 𝔪_P for its maximal ideal, κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P for its residue field, and the residue map for the quotient homomorphism O_P→κ(P). A divisor A is a function from all places of K to ℤ with finite support; inequalities between divisors mean inequalities of every coefficient, and A is effective if A(P)≥0 for every place P. Write deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P) and deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P), with the residue degrees cast to integers. Here Module.finrank is the natural-number-valued finite rank, which is the usual vector-space dimension when finite-dimensionality holds. For a place with discrete valuation ring O_P, ord_P(f) denotes the normalized integer order of f, positive on nonzero elements of 𝔪_P and negative on poles; its value at zero is defined to be ord_P(0)=0. Equivalently ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)), where v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ is the normalized multiplicative valuation, ℤᵐ⁰ is the multiplicative copy of ℤ with an added zero, and log and exp are the formal maps for this notation, not real analytic functions. Supply any proof hDVR that O_P is a discrete valuation ring for every place P of K. For each divisor A define the ℚ-subspace L(A)={f∈K | f=0 or ord_P(f)≥−A(P) for every place P} and ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A). Also supply a curve-field instance, meaning that there exists s∈K transcendental over ℚ with K finite-dimensional over ℚ(s). Write (f), (f)₀ and (f)∞ for the finite-support divisors of coefficients ord_P(f), max(0,ord_P(f)) and max(0,−ord_P(f)), respectively; these are the principal divisor, zero divisor and pole divisor of f. By the order convention all three divisors of the zero function are the zero divisor whose coefficients are all zero. Write [P] for the divisor of coefficient one at P and zero elsewhere. For every place P and π∈M.K with P.ord(π)=1, π is nonzero.

readbacks.en: For every natural number N and every given model M, let K=M.K be an intermediate field between ℚ and a fixed algebraic closure of the rational function field ℚ(X). The model supplies u,v∈K such that u is transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, K is finite-dimensional over ℚ(u), and [K:ℚ(u)]=N. A place P of K is a valuation subring O_P properly contained in K and containing the image of every rational number. Write 𝔪_P for its maximal ideal, κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P for its residue field, and the residue map for the quotient homomorphism O_P→κ(P). A divisor A is a function from all places of K to ℤ with finite support; inequalities between divisors mean inequalities of every coefficient, and A is effective if A(P)≥0 for every place P. Write deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P) and deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P), with the residue degrees cast to integers. Here Module.finrank is the natural-number-valued finite rank, which is the usual vector-space dimension when finite-dimensionality holds. For a place with discrete valuation ring O_P, ord_P(f) denotes the normalized integer order of f, positive on nonzero elements of 𝔪_P and negative on poles; its value at zero is defined to be ord_P(0)=0. Equivalently ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)), where v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ is the normalized multiplicative valuation, ℤᵐ⁰ is the multiplicative copy of ℤ with an added zero, and log and exp are the formal maps for this notation, not real analytic functions. Supply any proof hDVR that O_P is a discrete valuation ring for every place P of K. For each divisor A define the ℚ-subspace L(A)={f∈K | f=0 or ord_P(f)≥−A(P) for every place P} and ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A). Also supply a curve-field instance, meaning that there exists s∈K transcendental over ℚ with K finite-dimensional over ℚ(s). Write (f), (f)₀ and (f)∞ for the finite-support divisors of coefficients ord_P(f), max(0,ord_P(f)) and max(0,−ord_P(f)), respectively; these are the principal divisor, zero divisor and pole divisor of f. By the order convention all three divisors of the zero function are the zero divisor whose coefficients are all zero. Write [P] for the divisor of coefficient one at P and zero elsewhere. For every divisor A, place P and π∈M.K with P.ord(π)=1, define the ℚ-linear map L(A+[P])→κ(P) that sends f to the residue of π^(A(P)+1)f.

readbacks.en: For every natural number N and every given model M, let K=M.K be an intermediate field between ℚ and a fixed algebraic closure of the rational function field ℚ(X). The model supplies u,v∈K such that u is transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, K is finite-dimensional over ℚ(u), and [K:ℚ(u)]=N. A place P of K is a valuation subring O_P properly contained in K and containing the image of every rational number. Write 𝔪_P for its maximal ideal, κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P for its residue field, and the residue map for the quotient homomorphism O_P→κ(P). A divisor A is a function from all places of K to ℤ with finite support; inequalities between divisors mean inequalities of every coefficient, and A is effective if A(P)≥0 for every place P. Write deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P) and deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P), with the residue degrees cast to integers. Here Module.finrank is the natural-number-valued finite rank, which is the usual vector-space dimension when finite-dimensionality holds. For a place with discrete valuation ring O_P, ord_P(f) denotes the normalized integer order of f, positive on nonzero elements of 𝔪_P and negative on poles; its value at zero is defined to be ord_P(0)=0. Equivalently ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)), where v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ is the normalized multiplicative valuation, ℤᵐ⁰ is the multiplicative copy of ℤ with an added zero, and log and exp are the formal maps for this notation, not real analytic functions. Supply any proof hDVR that O_P is a discrete valuation ring for every place P of K. For each divisor A define the ℚ-subspace L(A)={f∈K | f=0 or ord_P(f)≥−A(P) for every place P} and ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A). Also supply a curve-field instance, meaning that there exists s∈K transcendental over ℚ with K finite-dimensional over ℚ(s). Write (f), (f)₀ and (f)∞ for the finite-support divisors of coefficients ord_P(f), max(0,ord_P(f)) and max(0,−ord_P(f)), respectively; these are the principal divisor, zero divisor and pole divisor of f. By the order convention all three divisors of the zero function are the zero divisor whose coefficients are all zero. Write [P] for the divisor of coefficient one at P and zero elsewhere. For every divisor A and place P, if L(A) is finite-dimensional over ℚ, then L(A+[P]) is finite-dimensional over ℚ and ℓ(A+[P])≤ℓ(A)+[κ(P):ℚ].

readbacks.en: For every natural number N and every given model M, let K=M.K be an intermediate field between ℚ and a fixed algebraic closure of the rational function field ℚ(X). The model supplies u,v∈K such that u is transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, K is finite-dimensional over ℚ(u), and [K:ℚ(u)]=N. A place P of K is a valuation subring O_P properly contained in K and containing the image of every rational number. Write 𝔪_P for its maximal ideal, κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P for its residue field, and the residue map for the quotient homomorphism O_P→κ(P). A divisor A is a function from all places of K to ℤ with finite support; inequalities between divisors mean inequalities of every coefficient, and A is effective if A(P)≥0 for every place P. Write deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P) and deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P), with the residue degrees cast to integers. Here Module.finrank is the natural-number-valued finite rank, which is the usual vector-space dimension when finite-dimensionality holds. For a place with discrete valuation ring O_P, ord_P(f) denotes the normalized integer order of f, positive on nonzero elements of 𝔪_P and negative on poles; its value at zero is defined to be ord_P(0)=0. Equivalently ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)), where v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ is the normalized multiplicative valuation, ℤᵐ⁰ is the multiplicative copy of ℤ with an added zero, and log and exp are the formal maps for this notation, not real analytic functions. Supply any proof hDVR that O_P is a discrete valuation ring for every place P of K. For each divisor A define the ℚ-subspace L(A)={f∈K | f=0 or ord_P(f)≥−A(P) for every place P} and ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A). Also supply a curve-field instance, meaning that there exists s∈K transcendental over ℚ with K finite-dimensional over ℚ(s). Write (f), (f)₀ and (f)∞ for the finite-support divisors of coefficients ord_P(f), max(0,ord_P(f)) and max(0,−ord_P(f)), respectively; these are the principal divisor, zero divisor and pole divisor of f. By the order convention all three divisors of the zero function are the zero divisor whose coefficients are all zero. Write [P] for the divisor of coefficient one at P and zero elsewhere. For every effective divisor D and every divisor A, if L(A) is finite-dimensional over ℚ, then L(A+D) is finite-dimensional over ℚ and ℓ(A+D)≤ℓ(A)+deg(D), with finranks cast to integers.

readbacks.en: For every natural number N and every given model M, let K=M.K be an intermediate field between ℚ and a fixed algebraic closure of the rational function field ℚ(X). The model supplies u,v∈K such that u is transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, K is finite-dimensional over ℚ(u), and [K:ℚ(u)]=N. A place P of K is a valuation subring O_P properly contained in K and containing the image of every rational number. Write 𝔪_P for its maximal ideal, κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P for its residue field, and the residue map for the quotient homomorphism O_P→κ(P). A divisor A is a function from all places of K to ℤ with finite support; inequalities between divisors mean inequalities of every coefficient, and A is effective if A(P)≥0 for every place P. Write deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P) and deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P), with the residue degrees cast to integers. Here Module.finrank is the natural-number-valued finite rank, which is the usual vector-space dimension when finite-dimensionality holds. For a place with discrete valuation ring O_P, ord_P(f) denotes the normalized integer order of f, positive on nonzero elements of 𝔪_P and negative on poles; its value at zero is defined to be ord_P(0)=0. Equivalently ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)), where v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ is the normalized multiplicative valuation, ℤᵐ⁰ is the multiplicative copy of ℤ with an added zero, and log and exp are the formal maps for this notation, not real analytic functions. Supply any proof hDVR that O_P is a discrete valuation ring for every place P of K. For each divisor A define the ℚ-subspace L(A)={f∈K | f=0 or ord_P(f)≥−A(P) for every place P} and ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A). Also supply a curve-field instance, meaning that there exists s∈K transcendental over ℚ with K finite-dimensional over ℚ(s). Assume deg((f))=0 for every f∈K. Write (f), (f)₀ and (f)∞ for the finite-support divisors of coefficients ord_P(f), max(0,ord_P(f)) and max(0,−ord_P(f)), respectively; these are the principal divisor, zero divisor and pole divisor of f. By the order convention all three divisors of the zero function are the zero divisor whose coefficients are all zero. Write [P] for the divisor of coefficient one at P and zero elsewhere. For every divisor A, L(A) is finite-dimensional over ℚ.

readbacks.en: For every natural number N and every given model M, let K=M.K be an intermediate field between ℚ and a fixed algebraic closure of the rational function field ℚ(X). The model supplies u,v∈K such that u is transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, K is finite-dimensional over ℚ(u), and [K:ℚ(u)]=N. A place P of K is a valuation subring O_P properly contained in K and containing the image of every rational number. Write 𝔪_P for its maximal ideal, κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P for its residue field, and the residue map for the quotient homomorphism O_P→κ(P). A divisor A is a function from all places of K to ℤ with finite support; inequalities between divisors mean inequalities of every coefficient, and A is effective if A(P)≥0 for every place P. Write deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P) and deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P), with the residue degrees cast to integers. Here Module.finrank is the natural-number-valued finite rank, which is the usual vector-space dimension when finite-dimensionality holds. For a place with discrete valuation ring O_P, ord_P(f) denotes the normalized integer order of f, positive on nonzero elements of 𝔪_P and negative on poles; its value at zero is defined to be ord_P(0)=0. Equivalently ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)), where v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ is the normalized multiplicative valuation, ℤᵐ⁰ is the multiplicative copy of ℤ with an added zero, and log and exp are the formal maps for this notation, not real analytic functions. Supply any proof hDVR that O_P is a discrete valuation ring for every place P of K. For each divisor A define the ℚ-subspace L(A)={f∈K | f=0 or ord_P(f)≥−A(P) for every place P} and ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A). Also supply a curve-field instance, meaning that there exists s∈K transcendental over ℚ with K finite-dimensional over ℚ(s). Assume deg((f))=0 for every f∈K. Write (f), (f)₀ and (f)∞ for the finite-support divisors of coefficients ord_P(f), max(0,ord_P(f)) and max(0,−ord_P(f)), respectively; these are the principal divisor, zero divisor and pole divisor of f. By the order convention all three divisors of the zero function are the zero divisor whose coefficients are all zero. Write [P] for the divisor of coefficient one at P and zero elsewhere. For every two divisors A≤B coefficientwise, deg(A)−ℓ(A)≤deg(B)−ℓ(B), interpreted over ℤ.

readbacks.en: For every natural number N and every given model M, let K=M.K be an intermediate field between ℚ and a fixed algebraic closure of the rational function field ℚ(X). The model supplies u,v∈K such that u is transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, K is finite-dimensional over ℚ(u), and [K:ℚ(u)]=N. A place P of K is a valuation subring O_P properly contained in K and containing the image of every rational number. Write 𝔪_P for its maximal ideal, κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P for its residue field, and the residue map for the quotient homomorphism O_P→κ(P). A divisor A is a function from all places of K to ℤ with finite support; inequalities between divisors mean inequalities of every coefficient, and A is effective if A(P)≥0 for every place P. Write deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P) and deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P), with the residue degrees cast to integers. Here Module.finrank is the natural-number-valued finite rank, which is the usual vector-space dimension when finite-dimensionality holds. For a place with discrete valuation ring O_P, ord_P(f) denotes the normalized integer order of f, positive on nonzero elements of 𝔪_P and negative on poles; its value at zero is defined to be ord_P(0)=0. Equivalently ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)), where v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ is the normalized multiplicative valuation, ℤᵐ⁰ is the multiplicative copy of ℤ with an added zero, and log and exp are the formal maps for this notation, not real analytic functions. Supply any proof hDVR that O_P is a discrete valuation ring for every place P of K. For each divisor A define the ℚ-subspace L(A)={f∈K | f=0 or ord_P(f)≥−A(P) for every place P} and ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A). Also supply a curve-field instance, meaning that there exists s∈K transcendental over ℚ with K finite-dimensional over ℚ(s). Assume deg((f))=0 for every f∈K. Write (f), (f)₀ and (f)∞ for the finite-support divisors of coefficients ord_P(f), max(0,ord_P(f)) and max(0,−ord_P(f)), respectively; these are the principal divisor, zero divisor and pole divisor of f. By the order convention all three divisors of the zero function are the zero divisor whose coefficients are all zero. Write [P] for the divisor of coefficient one at P and zero elsewhere. For every divisor A of negative degree, ℓ(A)=0.

readbacks.en: For every natural number N and every given model M, let K=M.K be an intermediate field between ℚ and a fixed algebraic closure of the rational function field ℚ(X). The model supplies u,v∈K such that u is transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, K is finite-dimensional over ℚ(u), and [K:ℚ(u)]=N. A place P of K is a valuation subring O_P properly contained in K and containing the image of every rational number. Write 𝔪_P for its maximal ideal, κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P for its residue field, and the residue map for the quotient homomorphism O_P→κ(P). A divisor A is a function from all places of K to ℤ with finite support; inequalities between divisors mean inequalities of every coefficient, and A is effective if A(P)≥0 for every place P. Write deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P) and deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P), with the residue degrees cast to integers. Here Module.finrank is the natural-number-valued finite rank, which is the usual vector-space dimension when finite-dimensionality holds. For a place with discrete valuation ring O_P, ord_P(f) denotes the normalized integer order of f, positive on nonzero elements of 𝔪_P and negative on poles; its value at zero is defined to be ord_P(0)=0. Equivalently ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)), where v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ is the normalized multiplicative valuation, ℤᵐ⁰ is the multiplicative copy of ℤ with an added zero, and log and exp are the formal maps for this notation, not real analytic functions. Supply any proof hDVR that O_P is a discrete valuation ring for every place P of K. For each divisor A define the ℚ-subspace L(A)={f∈K | f=0 or ord_P(f)≥−A(P) for every place P} and ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A). Also supply a curve-field instance, meaning that there exists s∈K transcendental over ℚ with K finite-dimensional over ℚ(s). Assume deg((f))=0 for every f∈K. Write (f), (f)₀ and (f)∞ for the finite-support divisors of coefficients ord_P(f), max(0,ord_P(f)) and max(0,−ord_P(f)), respectively; these are the principal divisor, zero divisor and pole divisor of f. By the order convention all three divisors of the zero function are the zero divisor whose coefficients are all zero. Write [P] for the divisor of coefficient one at P and zero elsewhere. For every divisor A with ℓ(A)≠0, there exists a nonzero f∈M.K belonging to L(A).

readbacks.en: For every natural number N and every given model M, let K=M.K be an intermediate field between ℚ and a fixed algebraic closure of the rational function field ℚ(X). The model supplies u,v∈K such that u is transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, K is finite-dimensional over ℚ(u), and [K:ℚ(u)]=N. A place P of K is a valuation subring O_P properly contained in K and containing the image of every rational number. Write 𝔪_P for its maximal ideal, κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P for its residue field, and the residue map for the quotient homomorphism O_P→κ(P). A divisor A is a function from all places of K to ℤ with finite support; inequalities between divisors mean inequalities of every coefficient, and A is effective if A(P)≥0 for every place P. Write deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P) and deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P), with the residue degrees cast to integers. Here Module.finrank is the natural-number-valued finite rank, which is the usual vector-space dimension when finite-dimensionality holds. For a place with discrete valuation ring O_P, ord_P(f) denotes the normalized integer order of f, positive on nonzero elements of 𝔪_P and negative on poles; its value at zero is defined to be ord_P(0)=0. Equivalently ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)), where v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ is the normalized multiplicative valuation, ℤᵐ⁰ is the multiplicative copy of ℤ with an added zero, and log and exp are the formal maps for this notation, not real analytic functions. Supply any proof hDVR that O_P is a discrete valuation ring for every place P of K. For each divisor A define the ℚ-subspace L(A)={f∈K | f=0 or ord_P(f)≥−A(P) for every place P} and ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A). Also supply a curve-field instance, meaning that there exists s∈K transcendental over ℚ with K finite-dimensional over ℚ(s). Assume deg((f))=0 for every f∈K. Write (f), (f)₀ and (f)∞ for the finite-support divisors of coefficients ord_P(f), max(0,ord_P(f)) and max(0,−ord_P(f)), respectively; these are the principal divisor, zero divisor and pole divisor of f. By the order convention all three divisors of the zero function are the zero divisor whose coefficients are all zero. Write [P] for the divisor of coefficient one at P and zero elsewhere. For every divisor A, ℓ(A)≤max(0,deg(A)+ℓ(0)), with finranks cast to integers.

readbacks.en: For every natural number N and every given model M, let K=M.K be an intermediate field between ℚ and a fixed algebraic closure of the rational function field ℚ(X). The model supplies u,v∈K such that u is transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, K is finite-dimensional over ℚ(u), and [K:ℚ(u)]=N. A place P of K is a valuation subring O_P properly contained in K and containing the image of every rational number. Write 𝔪_P for its maximal ideal, κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P for its residue field, and the residue map for the quotient homomorphism O_P→κ(P). A divisor A is a function from all places of K to ℤ with finite support; inequalities between divisors mean inequalities of every coefficient, and A is effective if A(P)≥0 for every place P. Write deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P) and deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P), with the residue degrees cast to integers. Here Module.finrank is the natural-number-valued finite rank, which is the usual vector-space dimension when finite-dimensionality holds. For a place with discrete valuation ring O_P, ord_P(f) denotes the normalized integer order of f, positive on nonzero elements of 𝔪_P and negative on poles; its value at zero is defined to be ord_P(0)=0. Equivalently ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)), where v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ is the normalized multiplicative valuation, ℤᵐ⁰ is the multiplicative copy of ℤ with an added zero, and log and exp are the formal maps for this notation, not real analytic functions. Supply any proof hDVR that O_P is a discrete valuation ring for every place P of K. For each divisor A define the ℚ-subspace L(A)={f∈K | f=0 or ord_P(f)≥−A(P) for every place P} and ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A). Write (f), (f)₀ and (f)∞ for the finite-support divisors of coefficients ord_P(f), max(0,ord_P(f)) and max(0,−ord_P(f)), respectively; these are the principal divisor, zero divisor and pole divisor of f. By the order convention all three divisors of the zero function are the zero divisor whose coefficients are all zero. Write [P] for the divisor of coefficient one at P and zero elsewhere. Write B=(u)∞ and C=Σ_i(b_i)∞ for the pole divisor of the model coordinate u and the fixed basis correction. Assume (i) deg((f))=0 for every f∈M.K; (ii) deg(B)=N as an integer; (iii) for every divisor A there exist nonzero z∈M.K and l∈ℕ with A+(z)≤lB coefficientwise; and (iv) for every l∈ℕ, (l+1)N≤ℓ(lB+C). Then there exist integers g₀,N₀ such that every divisor A of degree at least N₀ satisfies ℓ(A)=deg(A)−g₀ over ℤ.

readbacks.en: For every natural number N and every given model M, let K=M.K be an intermediate field between ℚ and a fixed algebraic closure of the rational function field ℚ(X). The model supplies u,v∈K such that u is transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, K is finite-dimensional over ℚ(u), and [K:ℚ(u)]=N. A place P of K is a valuation subring O_P properly contained in K and containing the image of every rational number. Write 𝔪_P for its maximal ideal, κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P for its residue field, and the residue map for the quotient homomorphism O_P→κ(P). A divisor A is a function from all places of K to ℤ with finite support; inequalities between divisors mean inequalities of every coefficient, and A is effective if A(P)≥0 for every place P. Write deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P) and deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P), with the residue degrees cast to integers. Here Module.finrank is the natural-number-valued finite rank, which is the usual vector-space dimension when finite-dimensionality holds. For a place with discrete valuation ring O_P, ord_P(f) denotes the normalized integer order of f, positive on nonzero elements of 𝔪_P and negative on poles; its value at zero is defined to be ord_P(0)=0. Equivalently ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)), where v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ is the normalized multiplicative valuation, ℤᵐ⁰ is the multiplicative copy of ℤ with an added zero, and log and exp are the formal maps for this notation, not real analytic functions. Supply any proof hDVR that O_P is a discrete valuation ring for every place P of K. For each divisor A define the ℚ-subspace L(A)={f∈K | f=0 or ord_P(f)≥−A(P) for every place P} and ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A). For every divisor A, ℓ(A)≤max(0,deg(A)+ℓ(0)), with the natural-valued finranks cast to integers.
readbacks.zh_Hans: 对任意自然数 N 和任意给定模型 M，令 K=M.K 为有理数域与有理函数域 ℚ(X) 的一个固定代数闭包之间的中间域。模型给定 u,v∈K，满足 u 关于有理数域超越、u^N+v^N=1、ℚ(u,v)=K、K 在 ℚ(u) 上有限维且 [K:ℚ(u)]=N。K 的一个处 P 指包含所有有理数的像且真包含于 K 的赋值子环 O_P。记 𝔪_P 为其极大理想，κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P 为其剩余域，剩余映射指商同态 O_P→κ(P)。除子 A 指 K 的全部处上的有限支撑整数值函数；除子不等式指每个处的系数不等式，若每个处 P 都满足 A(P)≥0，则称 A 有效。记 deg(P) 为剩余域 κ(P) 在有理数域上的自然数值有限秩，deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P)，其中剩余域次数先转为整数。自然数值有限秩在空间有限维时等于通常的向量空间维数。当处 P 的赋值环 O_P 为离散赋值环时，ord_P(f) 表示函数 f 的正规化整数阶，在极大理想的非零元素上为正、在极点处为负，并约定 ord_P(0)=0。等价地 ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f))，其中 v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ 为正规化乘法赋值，ℤᵐ⁰ 是整数加法群改写为乘法记法后再添零元的构造，log 与 exp 是该记法的形式映射，并非实数解析函数。另给定证明 hDVR，断言每个处 P 的赋值环 O_P 都是离散赋值环。对每个除子 A，定义有理数线性子空间 L(A)={f∈K | f=0 或每个处 P 都满足 ord_P(f)≥−A(P)}，并记 ℓ(A) 为 L(A) 在有理数域上的自然数值有限秩。对每个除子 A，将自然数值有限秩转为整数后，有 ℓ(A)≤max(0,deg(A)+ℓ(0))。
readbacks.ja: 任意の自然数 N と与えられた任意の模型 M に対し、K=M.K を有理数体と有理関数体 ℚ(X) の固定された代数閉包との間の中間体とする。模型は u,v∈K を与え、u は有理数体上超越的であり、u^N+v^N=1、ℚ(u,v)=K、K は ℚ(u) 上有限次元かつ [K:ℚ(u)]=N を満たす。K の素点 P とは、全ての有理数の像を含み K に真に含まれる付値部分環 O_P をいう。𝔪_P をその極大イデアル、κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P を剰余体とし、剰余写像は商準同型 O_P→κ(P) を表す。因子 A とは K の全ての素点上の有限台を持つ整数値関数である。因子の不等式は各係数の不等式を表し、全ての素点 P で A(P)≥0 なら A を有効という。deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P)、deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P) と書き、剰余体の次数は整数に型変換する。Module.finrank は自然数値の有限階数であり、空間が有限次元なら通常のベクトル空間の次元と一致する。O_P が離散付値環である素点では、ord_P(f) は f の正規化された整数値の位数を表し、極大イデアルの非零元では正、極では負となり、ord_P(0)=0 と定める。同値な表示は ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)) である。v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ は正規化された乗法的付値、ℤᵐ⁰ は整数の加法群を乗法的に書き零元を加えたものであり、log と exp はこの記法の形式的な写像であって実解析の関数ではない。全ての素点 P で O_P が離散付値環であることの任意の証明 hDVR を指定する。各因子 A に対し、有理数線形部分空間 L(A)={f∈K | f=0 または全ての素点 P で ord_P(f)≥−A(P)} を定め、ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A) と書く。任意の因子 A に対し、自然数値の有限階数を整数に型変換すると ℓ(A)≤max(0,deg(A)+ℓ(0)) が成立する。

readbacks.source_signature:
theorem riemannRochEventuallyLinear {N : ℕ} (M : Model N)
    (hDVR : PlacesDiscrete M) :
    ∃ g0 N0 : ℤ, ∀ A : Divisor M, N0 ≤ divisorDegree M A →
      (riemannEll M hDVR A : ℤ) = divisorDegree M A - g0
readbacks.full_signature:
theorem AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.riemannRochEventuallyLinear {N : ℕ} (M : Model N)
    (hDVR : PlacesDiscrete M) :
    ∃ g0 N0 : ℤ, ∀ A : Divisor M, N0 ≤ divisorDegree M A →
      (riemannEll M hDVR A : ℤ) = divisorDegree M A - g0

shape_questions_and_signature_boundaries.note: 三个新开放子声明的证明体均为 sorry。三个父声明源文件没有直接 sorry，但依赖这些开放子声明。本次不编译，不提供公理审查结论。
全部定义覆盖零函数；ord_P(0)=0，因此零函数的主除子、零点除子、极点除子均为零除子。
只对关于有理数域超越的函数断言零点和极点次数等于扩张次数；常数不是该签名的输入。principalDegreeZero_of_zeroPoleDegrees 的结论覆盖所有函数。
正式结论仅是自然数维数不等式。注释提到 u^k b_i 属于相应空间且线性无关，但签名不逐项输出这些性质；读回不将其提升为正式结论。hFinite 量化所有除子 A，不只量化 lB+C。
A 可为任意除子，不要求有效；z 必须非零，l 为自然数且允许零。z 和 l 可依赖 A。不等式为每个处的整数系数不等式。
基由 functionBasis 固定选取；修正除子为这组基的极点除子之和，调用者不另提供基或任意修正除子。基指标基数为实际扩张有限秩，模型字段另有该数等于 N。
namespace 内 include M hDVR hCurve 将这些 section 输入带入声明。PrincipalDegree section 又 include hDegreeZero；该条件已在完整签名与三语上下文展开。完整签名由源码重构，不是编译器输出。
该定义只是整数上的 sSup，不单独证明该集合有上界或上确界被取到；组合定理证明体中在几何输入下建立这些事实。正式组合结论仍是存在整数常数的最终线性公式。
hDegreeZero 对所有函数量化；hPoleDegree 精确为模型坐标 u 的极点除子次数等于整数 N；hApprox 对所有除子量化；hBasis 对所有自然数 l 量化。组合签名不额外接受 hFinite，局部证明链由 hDegreeZero 导出有限维。
g₀、N₀ 为整数且无正性约束；最终线性对全部足够大次数除子有效，不要求有效。上界仍使用实际 ℓ(0)，没有将其设为一，也没有将 g₀ 识别为几何亏格减一。
所有声明量化任意自然数 N 和给定 Model N，不加入模型存在性或 N 的额外下界。
英文原文引文与经核实定位待主代理补充，没有编造论文原文引用。
